A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original LoRA training results, compression evaluations, reconstruction analyses, and measured throughput from simulated multi-LoRA serving.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds 1,000-LoRA compression results, heterogeneous-rank experiments, cross-task privacy tests, and memory and timing measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix A retain the JD-Full/JD-Diag objectives, alternating and eigenvalue solvers, and clustering updates. Added kernel pseudocode and deployment recommendations expand implementation documentation without establishing a change to the proposed compression procedure.

E1.justification: Training coverage expands from v2's 500 English-only Natural Instructions tasks to v3's reported 1,000-task collection. Table 3 includes Bengali-Hindi translation and Bengali sentiment classification, establishing broader language and task coverage. The ten primary compression-evaluation tasks remain unchanged. Appendix C inconsistently retains the earlier 500-task, English-only description.

E2.justification: v3 Appendix E newly reports implementing and evaluating F-LoRA, finding no forward-pass speed advantage over standard LoRA; v2 discusses it only conceptually. The existing TIES, SVD, base-model, uncompressed-LoRA, and vLLM comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include ranks sampled from 16-64 with a rank-43 control, joint-versus-separate compression controls, and timing measurements separating all 96 modules' memory usage from single-module transfer and computation. For the existing 1,024-LoRA serving point, v2 Appendix E specifies seven rank-64 clusters and 60 resident baseline adapters; v3 Appendix F specifies 25 rank-16 clusters and 28 baseline adapters. This establishes a reported setting revision, not that measurements were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix H.1 tests heterogeneous-rank compression against a matched-parameter, uniform-rank control across cluster counts. H.2 investigates cross-task transfer under joint versus separate compression, while Appendix E separates memory, transfer, and forward-pass costs. Existing random-matrix, convergence, and LoRA-hub analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Tables 7-14 add uncertainty values to the 100-LoRA, five- and seven-cluster results that appeared as point estimates in v2 Tables 3-10. Both versions already state three runs with different seeds; v3 does not explicitly increase that count or introduce significance testing.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for 1,000 compressed LoRAs, including average relative ROUGE-L of 1.00 with a total parameter-saving ratio of 0.97 in Table 7, alongside new rank, privacy, and timing outcomes. Existing clustering results also change: the 100-LoRA, five-cluster relative ROUGE-L average changes from 1.02 to 1.04 ± 0.08. Table 1's aggregate LoRA ROUGE-L changes from 76.22 to 67.80 across different task collections, so this is not a same-setting decline.

T1.justification: Proposition 1, Theorem 1, Corollary 1, the algorithm derivations, and Appendix B's proof retain their mathematical content. Changes such as replacing the cluster-count notation with k are not substantive theoretical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract expands the advertised empirical validation from 500 to 1,000 LoRAs, and the introduction expands the trained-adapter contribution to over 1,000. The central compression, clustering, reconstruction-bound, performance-preservation, and 1.6-times/80% throughput claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds a memory-transfer explanation of serving gains with unchanged forward-pass latency, greater reconstruction-error tolerance under clustering, and practical applicability recommendations. Section 7 also introduces a privacy interpretation suggesting no cross-task gains or leakage. That interpretation overstates Table 6: task280's average cross-task ROUGE-L is 35.64 when compressed together versus 24.83 separately.

D1.justification: v3 adds an adapter-collection access link, the full task-ID list, and Punica integration pseudocode in Appendix F.4. Section 6.5 supplies explicit rank/cluster-selection guidance, a 0.6 reconstruction-loss threshold, and recommendations for background CPU recompression. These substantially expand reproducibility and deployment information beyond v2's general guidance; the code release remains a promise.

R1.justification: Related work adds Punica and VeRA and explains compression's complementary relationship to serving kernels and alternative PEFT approaches. The new discussion of (IA)3 concerns a Liu et al. work already cited in v2. The overall research positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The original section sequence and narrative remain, with sentence-level tightening, shortened headings, new Benefits and Recommendations subsections, and an Impact Statement. Appendix commentary is consolidated ahead of the detailed result tables.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns. Figure 2 is redesigned from savings versus collection size to performance versus savings; Figures 3-4 revise plotted content, scales, and presentation. New timing and ablation displays appear, Table 1 moves to Appendix C, and detailed benchmark tables receive larger, separate-page layouts.

improvement.justification: The added 1,000-LoRA results, heterogeneous-rank control, timing breakdown, and implementation guidance strengthen validation and practical usability beyond v2. The overall gain is limited: primary compression evaluation retains the same ten tasks, Appendix C contradicts the expanded training description, and the new privacy interpretation overstates Table 6's mixed cross-task findings.
